en: Homage to the Blessed One, the Heart of the Noble Mahāgaṇapati! Homage to the Triple Gem!

Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak Mountain, together with a great community of monks consisting of twelve hundred and fifty monks, and with many Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas. Now at that time, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda.
O noble son Ānanda, whoever shall uphold, recite, master, and propagate these heart-mantras of Gaṇapati, all his undertakings will be successfully accomplished.
Oṃ, homage be to you, the Great Gaṇapati, svāhā!
Oṃ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ!
Oṃ, homage to Gaṇapati, svāhā! Oṃ, homage to the Lord of the Gaṇas, svāhā! Oṃ, homage to Gaṇeśvara, svāhā!
Oṃ, to her who is worshipped by Gaṇapati, svāhā!

Oṃ kaṭa kaṭa maṭa maṭa dara dara vidara vidara hana hana gṛhṇa gṛhṇa dhāva dhāva bhañja bhañja jambha jambha tambha tambha stambha stambha moha moha deha deha dadāpaya dadāpaya! Grant me the accomplishment of wealth!
Oṃ, to the incarnation of Rudra, svāhā!
Oṃ, the Great Laughter, which agitates the mind with the wondrous drop, is arriving!
To the one of great fear, great power, and great prowess, who bestows [gifts] with his great hand, grant [this], svāhā!
Oṃ, homage be to you, Mahāgaṇapati; svāhā!
Oṃ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ gaḥ!
Oṃ, homage to Gaṇapati; svāhā!
Oṃ, svāhā to Gaṇeśvara! Oṃ, svāhā to Gaṇādhipati! Oṃ, svāhā to the one worshipped by Gaṇapati!
Oṃ suru suru svāhā / Oṃ turu turu svāhā / Oṃ muru muru svāhā /
These, Ānanda, are the heart-mantras of Gaṇapati.

Whosoever— a son of noble family or a daughter of noble family, a monk or a nun, a layman or a laywoman— who undertakes any task, whether it be the accomplishment of a mantra, worship of the Triple Gem, traveling to another region, entering the royal court, or becoming invisible— should, having performed worship to the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, [recite] the Heart of the Noble Gaṇapati.
It should be recited seven times; all his undertakings will be accomplished, of this there is no doubt.
Among all strife, quarrels, oppression, and envy, it should always be recited for pacification; everything will become completely stilled.
Rising every day, one should recite it seven times for an entire kalpa; one will become possessed of great good fortune.
When he goes to the royal court, he will possess great palaces;
he will be one who retains what he has heard;
and no great diseases will arise in his body.
No one who circumambulates Tārā will find an opportunity for harm; even a bee shall find no opening, nor shall there be any obstacles to their supreme thought of awakening (bodhicitta).
In birth after birth, they will remember their past lives.

Thus spoke the Blessed One; and those monks, those bodhisattvas mahāsattvas, and that entire assembly, including the world with its gods, humans, asuras, garuḍas, and gandharvas, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
The Noble Heart-Mantra of Mahāgaṇapati is completed.
